title: Ingress fallback provenance matrix and graceful handover
content:
Context:
This is a personal scratchpad for defining a minimal, debuggable provenance envelope to attach to requests that are routed to fallback variants (model shards, regions, cheaper quantized variants, or onboarded local runtimes).

Goal:
- Define an API-friendly provenance header/body shape that preserves traceability and minimal semantics for safe handover.
- Specify operator config for graceful handover policies and a matrix mapping failure / load modes -> actions + telemetry to emit.
- Capture open questions and quick experiments to validate.

Why:
Current problem: when requests are rerouted (capacity pressure, regional outage, model-level failure), we frequently lose the call-site context about what triggered the handover and what pre-handover route looked like. That makes debugging customer incidents and correlating regressions (in quality or cost) hard.

Design constraints: (tradeoffs)
- Small: header should be compact so it doesn't blow up p99 bandwidth for streaming.
- Machine-parsable: easy to index and filter in logs/metrics.
- Human-readable on inspection (console) for quick RCA.
- Non-sensitive: avoid sending PII in the header; preserve only routing/provenance semantics.
- Backwards compatible: when header absent, system behaves as today.

Proposal: X-Redwood-Fallback-Provenance (structured header OR base64 compact)
- two acceptable encodings: structured serialized JSON (for internal clients) or base64url(json) (for external/edge proxies)
- header name: X-Redwood-Fallback-Provenance

Schema (informal JSON):
{
  "trace_id": "string (global request trace)",
  "ingress_route": "string (e.g. hosted/us-east-1/api-gw-v2)",
  "prior_model": "string (model-id@variant)",
  "fallback_reason": "enum(capacity_pressure | region_down | model_error | quality_regression | operator_override)",
  "trigger_ts": "iso8601",
  "decision_policy_id": "string | null",
  "fallback_target": "string (target route / model)",
  "handover_meta": "optional small map: policy_ttl, priority_hint, graceful_window_s",
  "sampled_debug_token": "short-id to look up full trace in debugstore (optional)"
}

Example header (compact):
X-Redwood-Fallback-Provenance: 

Operator config sketch (YAML-like):
handover_policies:
  - id: pf-7
    description: fallback to quantized-cpu pool when >90% GPU queue latency or during maintenance windows
    trigger_conditions:
      - type: queue_latency
        threshold_ms: 2500
      - type: scheduled_maintenance
    actions:
      - type: route_to
        target: quant-v2-cpu
      - type: emit_telemetry
        telemetry_tags: [fallback, quant, grace-mode]
    graceful_window_s: 45
    sample_debug: 1/1000

Handover matrix (failure mode -> action -> telemetry to capture):
- capacity_pressure -> immediate route_to cheaper_pool / enqueue -> emit {fallback_reason, prior_model, queue_snapshot, sampled_debug_token}
- region_down -> route_to region-fallback -> emit {fallback_reason, prior_route, region, decision_policy_id}
- model_error (OOM / kernel crash) -> try pinned-variant v-rollback -> if still failing, route_to smaller-context model -> emit {prior_model, error_code, runtime_logs_link}
- operator_override -> route_to operator-specified -> emit {operator_id, override_ticket}

ASCII sequence diagram (simplified):
Client -> Ingress: request w/o provenance header
Ingress -> RoutingService: evaluate capacity -> decision: fallback? yes -> RoutingService sets provenance header -> RoutingService -> TargetPool: request with X-Redwood-Fallback-Provenance
TargetPool -> Response: include X-Redwood-Fallback-Provenance in response for visibility

Notes on telemetry and storage:
- Keep the provenance content small. The sampled_debug_token is used to look up full expanded payload in a separate debug-store (retention short, encrypted).
- Metrics: expose counter by (fallback_reason, decision_policy_id) and histogram of fallback_duration_s (time from trigger_ts to end of request).

API/SDK ergonomics:
- SDKs should offer helpers: attach_provenance(ctx, reason, decision_id, fallback_target) -> automatically populate trace_id from context
- CLI/console: show provenance column in recent traces view; clicking token opens a debug pane (if retained)

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to safely represent multi-hop fallback? (e.g. chained handovers). Idea: short chain array but capped depth=3.
- Privacy review: confirm no sensitive request text or user ids slip into header; if unavoidable, always store only a hash (and keep it internal).
- Sampling policy for sampled_debug_token: default 1/1000, but override for enterprise customers or SLO-critical routes.
- Interop: edge proxies may not accept long structured headers; confirm size limits across common CDNs. If too large, prefer base64 compact encoding or put compact token and use sidechannel to store full map.

Quick experiment plan:
1) Implement a cheap proof-of-concept in a canary route: produce header with {trace_id, prior_model, fallback_reason, decision_policy_id} and optional sampled_debug_token (write to debugstore with TTL=1h).
2) Instrument metrics and a dashboard: fallback counts by route + 95th p99 for the fallback duration.
3) Run synthetic traffic to force capacity_pressure and validate the chain is preserved end-to-end and searchable in logs.

Decision log (short-term):
- Encoding: allow both JSON and base64url(JSON) (fallback to base64 if header length > 512 bytes).
- Required fields: [trace_id, fallback_reason, trigger_ts, fallback_target]. Everything else optional.

If this proves useful, next steps: formalize header schema in the public API docs (hosted-api team) and add a small SDK helper in python/js to manage provenance lifecycle.

Notes-to-self: reach out to @Rajat (runtime-telemetry) and @Maya (console) to align on UI footprint and storage TTL. Put a spike ticket (ENG-6123) to track.

End of scratchpad.
